R1.outcome: group-land drift and inner-push non_fast_forward now resetGroup (re-queue) instead of rejectGroup, matching what the single-repo lane has always done for the identical event. auth/network/other still reject. Bounded at 4 integration attempts, DERIVED from a real member's attempt rows (no migration); past the bound it rejects with a reason naming lane contention rather than the change. An unreadable count re-queues anyway.
R1.expected_impact: This is the fix for the reported 'main moved and it got rejected' pain.

R2.why: Premise verified false. worktree.resetForAttempt() (worktree.ts:148-154) fetches and hard-resets to origin/main before EVERY attempt and assembleGroup reads its base immediately after, so every rebase already runs against fresh main — a retry would hit the identical conflict. The real staleness window (main moving during a 30-min verify) is already covered by R1's re-queue. A conflict surviving that is REAL and belongs to R4.

R3.outcome: A reject raises an escalation addressed to the submitting worker (originWorkerKey from their keyed agent_claims binding), so the existing wake daemon delivers it into their session. New setting `notify_author_on_reject`, ships OFF.
R3.trap_pinned: The daemon delivers 'messages NOT authored by the origin author'. Authoring the escalation as the integrator — the natural way to write it — would make the notice self-authored, match nothing, and wake nobody, SILENTLY. So the escalation belongs to the worker and the notice comes from the train; a test pins exactly that.
R3.design_note: Its own raise path, not create(): create() sets authorId from the actor (wrong end) and its FTS dedup would fold two different rejections into one thread, losing an outcome.

verification.integrator: group-land 9/9 (incl. 3 new R1 tests), group suites 48/48, batch + assembly + recovery + seal 127/127
verification.gates: typecheck + lint + format:check + build all pass; openapi + api-types regenerated through the drift guard

remaining.R4: The cross-repo resolver executor. Blockers unchanged: createResolverPool is single-repo (needs correlated inner+outer worktrees); merge_resolutions is single-origin (a group has two origins and must resubmit a group); hasRemainingMarkers() is conflict-marker shaped and meaningless for gitlink_diverged. Cheapest shape: inner_conflict → resolve in an inner worktree → resubmit as an INNER-ONLY group (synthesize_outer). This is the only large step in the campaign.
remaining.R5: Wire rejectGroupLegibly → maybeOpenResolution behind assemblyResolutionEligibility (the gate shipped in the previous campaign; the hook is deliberately unwired until R4 can execute what it opens), plus docs and the full seal.

deployment: No migration in this campaign. A PM-server redeploy picks up the R3 setting and the reject notification; the daemon needs a rebundle + restart for R1. notify_author_on_reject must be turned ON per project before any escalation is raised.
